question: Generally, with development, the share of agricultural sector ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**decreases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As economies develop, there is a structural shift from agriculture to industry and services, leading to a decrease in the agricultural sector's share in GDP.
 
• This shift is attributed to higher productivity and income levels in the industrial and service sectors compared to agriculture.
 
• Employment also moves from agriculture to more productive sectors, further reducing the agricultural sector's contribution.
 
• Developed countries typically have a very small percentage of their workforce employed in agriculture compared to developing countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Development:**

 
 
• Economic development is the process by which the overall health, well-being, and academic level of the general population improves.
 
• It involves a transition from primary activities like agriculture to secondary and tertiary activities like manufacturing and services.
 
 
 
• **GDP Composition:**
 
 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) composition by sector typically includes agriculture, industry, and services.
 
• In developed economies, the service sector often dominates GDP composition.
 
 
 
• **Labor Shift:**
 
 
• As countries develop, labor shifts from agriculture to more productive sectors, resulting in higher wages and better living standards.
 
• This shift is driven by technological advancements and increased educational opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Productivity:**
 
 
• Productivity in agriculture is generally lower than in industry and services, which leads to a natural shift as countries develop.
 
• Higher productivity in non-agricultural sectors attracts labor and investment, reducing agriculture's share.
